title: Accessing and Slicing Python Lists
learningObjectives: Explain the behavior of accessing and slicing python lists.
Select appropriate list operations for a given task.
Predict the effect of indexing, mutation and copying.
Write readable code that processes list data.
Avoid common list-related errors and side effects.

understand.concept: List indexes access individual items. Indexing starts at zero, and negative indexes count from the end. Slicing uses list[start:stop:step] to create a new list containing selected items; the stop index is excluded. An invalid individual index raises IndexError, while slices safely clamp many out-of-range boundaries.
understand.whyItMatters: Indexing and slicing let a program retrieve a specific item or a useful portion of a sequence.
understand.analogy: Indexing is like opening one numbered drawer; slicing is like taking a selected run of drawers.
understand.analogyLimit: A slice creates a new list containing references to the selected elements; it is a shallow copy, not a deep copy.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Positive indexes

The first item is at index zero. Use `items[0]` for the first item.

## 2. Negative indexes

`items[-1]` accesses the last item, and `items[-2]` accesses the second-last.

## 3. Slices

`items[start:stop]` includes start and excludes stop. A step can select every nth item or reverse a sequence.

## 4. Index errors

An individual index outside the valid range raises IndexError.

practise.guidedTask: Print the first item, last item and middle slice from a list of at least five values.
practise.independentTask: Given a list of ten values, create slices for the first three, last three and every second value. Explain why the stop index is excluded.
hints: A slice excludes its stop index.
The step controls how indexes advance.
Use a negative step to reverse.
practise.challenge: Predict the output of several slices with omitted start/stop values and negative steps. Explain which slices create new lists.

questions.prompt: What is the index of the first list item?

questions.explanation: Negative one refers to the final element.

questions.prompt: Is the stop index included in a slice?
questions.explanation: The slice stop boundary is exclusive.
A negative step traverses the sequence backwards.

questions.prompt: What happens when an individual list index is out of range?
questions.explanation: Accessing a nonexistent index raises IndexError.
